significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish both a causal mechanism and a form-(iii) predictive coupling: accepted and superseded mechanisms exist as competing, separable representations, steering one changes the stated mechanism, and the "correct-vs-superseded probe-strength ratio predicts" outdated reasoning on other questions. This fixes more than the existence of scientific concepts: it explains a structured class of errors and predicts which mechanisms and models will exhibit them; the phenomenon is context-sensitive regression to coherent obsolete theories, while the proposed mechanism is competition between their internal representations. TruthfulQA (Lin et al., 2022) operationalizes imitation of human misconceptions behaviorally, while latent-knowledge work such as Burns et al. (2023) relies on internal signals, so establishing or rejecting this specific representation-to-error coupling would materially constrain both explanations and diagnostics; however, because the hypothesis conjoins separability, causation, and prediction, a generic negative result may reject the package without ruling out nonlinear or noncompetitive legacy representations. Verified-true and verified-false states are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check passes: replacing historical-theory competition with the generic topic would remove the causal and predictive law supporting an above-median score.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "correct-vs-superseded probe-strength ratio," the "theory-competition diagnostic," and the per-model "legacy-theory susceptibility" score. These are ex-ante predictors because the claim says the ratio predicts "the model's default answer and its error rate on held-out mechanistic questions," leaving auditors or dataset curators an action window before relying on those answers rather than merely explaining failures afterward. After re-extraction on another model, the claimed predictive relation still says what should be found—greater relative legacy-theory strength should forecast outdated outputs—although the individual activation directions and calibration values would remain model-specific; asserted scope spans scientific and general model families and mechanisms in chemistry, biology, medicine, and physics. The downstream users can include people auditing, curating, or gating scientific-model deployment, and the topic-substitution check passes because the generic scientific-representation topic supplies neither this predictor nor a legacy-theory screening handle.
